maya: Quick design question — Figma link with two options: dense spend rows with inline token counts vs lighter rows + chart heavy. Which should get visual priority? https://www.figma.com/file/abc123 (screenshot attached) kevin: i prefer lighter rows + chart. gives better visual hierarchy. dense rows feel like a ledger and compete with charts :thinking: sarah: from perf side, inline token breakdowns mean more DOM nodes when list is long. if we go inline we should virtualize or lazy-render details. lucas: also think about invoice CTA placement. In dense rows we have space to put a small download icon per row, but that gets noisy. In chart-first view maybe a persistent invoice button in header + per-row "more" menu? maya: good points. question: when you hover a row in chart-first view, do we show a compact hover card with token split and download? or require expand/click? kevin: hover card is nice for mouse users, but keyboard-only and mobile need click-to-expand. hover-only is a11y anti-pattern. prefer hover for discoverability + click to pin. design-bot: snapshot-tests: spend-list-hover-card v3 -> baseline diff 0.03% :white_check_mark: sarah: for keyboard, we need a clear focus target. Suggest making the entire row a single focusable element with aria-expanded state and an enter/space toggle. sample ARIA snippet: ```
...
``` kevin: agree. also iconography — download vs invoice wording. "Download invoice" vs "Download CSV" vs just a file icon. copy matters for new users. lucas: what about a global scope toggle (Org / Project) affecting the chart aggregations and the invoice CTA behavior? in org scope the invoice should default to account-level invoice in header, project scope shows per-project invoice in row. maya: yeah that's in the spec but we need visual affordances to make scope obvious. maybe a subtle breadcrumb: "Org > Project" with small invoice CTA aligned right. sarah: accessibility nit: ensure color contrast for the small token badges is >=4.5:1. also token counts should not rely on color alone — include labels or icons. kevin: alternative interaction thought — inline accordion that expands pushes list down (good for mobile) vs overlay popover that floats over (better for keeping scroll position). which one do we prefer? maya: mobile-first -> accordion. desktop -> popover/hover-card. keep interaction parity: both expose same actions (download, view details, pin to drawer). lucas: actionable next steps: kevin -> update Figma with hover + focus states; sarah -> perf estimate for lazy render; maya -> write copy variants for CTA ("Download invoice", "Export billing CSV", "Get invoice PDF"); i'll sync with PMs on scope toggle language. kevin: will do, pushing Figma update by EOD. :rocket: sarah: i'll have quick perf numbers by tomorrow noon. maya: thanks all — i'll schedule a short review tomorrow 10am PT. :thumbsup:
